heard: A Soviet lander sent signals from Venus long past its death sentence. On 1 March 1982, Vaynera 13 plunged into 89 atmospheres of crushing pressure. With ground temperatures at 457 degrees Celsius, engineers designed it to last approximately 32 minutes. Yet it kept transmitting, capturing the first acoustic sound recordings ever made on another world. Its drilling arm pulled soil into an internal chamber, kept at 30 degrees Celsius. The lander beamed back the first color panoramas of Venus, sparking claims of alien creatures. Photo analysts soon proved that mysterious moving organism was just the probe's ejected lens cap. Venera 13 defied the crushing furnace, transmitting vital data for 127 minutes. Soviet Mission Control had only expected it to survive for 32 minutes.
